items.title: South Cotabato campus gun attack planned a month prior
items.description: The student who killed two schoolmates with a pistol and wounded six others in a shooting incident inside a school campus in Banga, South Cotabato, on Friday, September 18, had long planned the attack, and his friends knew about it.

items.title: ‘Deep dark web’ influenced South Cotabato school shooter — DILG
items.description: The student who opened fire at Banga National High School in South Cotabato had been heavily involved in activities on the “deep dark web,” Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla said Saturday.

items.title: South Cotabato school shooter used DepEd employee father’s gun
items.description: A Grade 9 student who opened fire at Banga National High School in South Cotabato used his father’s firearm, Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla said.

items.title: No justification for China Coast Guard to ram BFAR vessel — DFA
items.description: The Department of Foreign Affairs said there was no justification for a China Coast Guard vessel to ram a Philippine civilian vessel conducting a humanitarian mission in the West Philippine Sea.

items.title: Possible EV link in June Aster fire prompts ferry bans, safety review
items.description: Shipping firms impose restrictions as the June Aster fire investigation continues.

items.title: Philippines tagged as deadliest Asian country for environmentalists
items.description: The Philippines was named as the deadliest country in Asia for environmental defenders for the 13th consecutive year, climate justice watchdog Global Witness reported.

items.title: House prosecutors defend statements on impeachment
items.description: Members of the House prosecution panel have maintained that their statements on the ongoing impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte were not about the merits of the case, but merely on procedure and summary of the proceedings.

items.title: Shipping firm bans EVs on board
items.description: Domestic shipping company Montenegro Shipping Lines Inc. has banned the loading of electric and hybrid vehicles aboard its vessels following recent findings on the ferry MV June Aster, which caught fire off Coron, Palawan last week.

items.title: Villar family faces graft complaints over PrimeWater deals
items.description: The Office of the Ombudsman filed criminal and administrative complaints against members of the Villar family yesterday over allegedly disadvantageous joint venture agreements of PrimeWater Infrastructure Corp. with local water districts.

items.title: Tropical storm forms outside PAR
items.description: The tropical cyclone outside the Philippine area of responsibility (PAR), with the international name Dujuan, has developed into a severe tropical storm, the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (PAGASA) said yesterday.

items.title: Globe brings 917 GDay 2026 Love Overload closer to communities nationwide
items.description: Globe is taking 917 GDay 2026 closer to customers. This year’s Love Overload will be showing up in the neighborhoods, convergence areas, and events through a series of GDay pop-ups from September to October across Luzon, Visayas, and Mindanao. This year, GDay Love Overload will make stops in Quezon City, General Trias, Cebu, Lucena, Bacolod […]

items.title: Watchdog identifies P970-billion in ‘red flags’ within proposed 2027 budget
items.description: The People’s Budget Coalition (PBC) said it has identified P970 billion in red flag items within the government’s proposed P7.2-trillion national budget for 2027, citing risks of political patronage, waste, and unvetted infrastructure insertions. The network of watchdog and research groups had earlier flagged P735.56 billion in the 2027 National Expenditure Program as vulnerable to […]

items.title: Ombudsman files graft raps vs Villars over PrimeWater deals
items.description: The Office of the Ombudsman has filed graft and administrative complaints against members of the Villar family and other officials over allegedly poor water service under joint venture agreements between PrimeWater Infrastructure Corp. (PWIC) and local water districts. A report from the Office of the Government Corporate Counsel showed that 75 local water districts entered […]

items.title: Malaysia optimistic on PHL tourism market despite fuel surcharge rise
items.description: Malaysia remains optimistic about the Philippines as a key tourism source market despite higher fuel surcharges that could raise travel costs for Filipino visitors, according to a Malaysian diplomat. “For the Philippines, I think last year we touched almost 500,000. Of course, we’re looking to increase it,” Malaysian Ambassador Abdul Malik Melvin Castelino Anthony told […]

items.title: STARLUX Airlines projects triple-digit passenger growth in 2026
items.description: Taiwan’s STARLUX Airlines said that it is projecting ‘triple-digit’ passenger growth in 2026, up from approximately 75% recorded a year earlier, as it expands services in the Philippines. “From 2025 to 2026, we achieved record growth of around 75% compared to last year,” STARLUX Airlines Manager Jan Claude Angco told reporters in an interview on […]

items.title: UP to ask lawmakers to restore P29.5-billion budget
items.description: Amid a looming P2.95-billion budget cut for the University of the Philippines (UP) under the 2027 proposed budget, the university will ask lawmakers to restore its P29.5-billion budget from last year to prioritize the completion of buildings under construction and strengthen its research capacity, according to its top official on Friday. “There is a budget […]

items.title: Tony Parker finds familiar passion in Philippines return
items.description: Tony Parker has traveled the world through basketball, but only twice has that journey brought him to the Philippines. A decade after his first visit, one thing still stood out to the four-time NBA champion above everything else. “The people,” Parker said during a visit to the ArenaPlus booth at the inaugural NBA House Philippines […]

items.title: French prosecutors and regulators step up scrutiny on smart glasses
items.description: PARIS — Paris prosecutors have opened a criminal probe into suspected sexual harassment involving smart glasses, while French data protection authorities have received complaints from businesses, as countries around the world grapple with the devices’ social impact. There are several smart glasses available, but US tech giant Meta’s glasses made in collaboration with EssilorLuxottica are […]

items.description: MANILA is hopeful for a positive response from Washington as negotiations continue over the 12.5% US tariff imposed on Philippine exports due to concerns over goods allegedly tied to forced labor imports. At a news briefing ahead of the upcoming 58th ASEAN Economic Ministers’ Meeting held on Friday, Trade Undersecretary Allan B. Gepty said the […]

items.title: VIOMI Philippines unveils global smart water filter innovations for Filipino homes and businesses
items.description: Global AI water technology brand VIOMI Philippines introduces its first three smart water filter models designed to provide Filipino households and businesses with advanced filtration technology, intelligent features, and a more convenient drinking water experience. During the VIOMI Philippines Founding Partner Dinner, Mr. Khelvin P. Cruz presented the brand’s initial product lineup featuring the VIOMI […]

items.title: Taiwan Excellence Pavilion 2026 brings innovation and business opportunities to Manila
items.description: Taiwan’s latest innovations are taking center stage in Manila as the Taiwan Excellence Pavilion opens during Taiwan Expo 2026, running from Sept. 17 to 19 at the SMX Convention Center in Pasay City. items.title: Puregold marks 28 years of retail growth, gives back to loyal customers
items.description: Marking 28 years of sustained retail growth and market leadership, leading supermarket chain Puregold Price Club, Inc. is launching a grand anniversary celebration this September, giving away exciting rewards designed to make every loyal customer feel valued. Puregold’s anniversary celebration rollout comes as it marks a 3.7% year-on-year sales growth in the first half of […]

items.title: KGOC Sportsfest The Finale 2026: Seven years of unity, strength, and care for employees
items.description: The Kryzl Group of Companies (KGOC) successfully held “KGOC Sportsfest The Finale 2026,” marking the colorful conclusion of its annual sports competition for employees. For seven years, KGOC has continued to organize the Sportsfest as part of its commitment to employee welfare. The event provides employees with an opportunity to take a break from their […]

items.title: LPA hits Palawan, affects Visayas and other areas amid storm Dujuan
items.description: A low pressure area (LPA) is affecting Palawan and causing thunderstorms in seven areas, posing a risk of flash floods and landslides amid the continued presence of severe tropical storm Dujuan, the state weather bureau said on Friday. “The LPA was located over Dumaran, Palawan and is currently traversing Palawan,” Leanne Loreto, weather specialist of […]

items.title: DoE terminates coal block auction
items.description: THE DEPARTMENT of Energy (DoE) will no longer pursue its planned coal block auction this year, which would have included the country’s largest mine operated by Semirara Mining and Power Corp. (SMPC).

items.title: Philippine growth seen picking up in second half — World Bank
items.description: PHILIPPINE ECONOMIC growth could pick up in the second half as public infrastructure spending accelerates and inflation eases, bringing the government’s full-year growth target within closer reach, a World Bank economist said.

items.title: OFW remittances in peril amid Middle East war risks
items.description: REMITTANCE FLOWS from overseas Filipino workers (OFWs) are likely to remain subdued until yearend as overseas deployment slows and renewed hostilities in the Middle East create more volatility, banks said.

items.title: NSCR full operations pushed back to 2033
items.description: THE North-South Commuter Railway (NSCR) is now targeted to be fully operational by 2033 after the Economy and Development (ED) Council approved amendments to the project, with partial operations expected to start in December 2027. The full operations of the NSCR are now targeted to start by the third quarter of 2033, later than the […]

items.title: IV of Spades takes top Awit Award nods
items.description: THE four-piece band IV of Spades took home the top prizes — Song of the Year for “Aura” and Album of the Year for Andalucia — at this year’s Awit Awards which were held on Sept. 15 at the SM Mall of Asia Arena in Pasay City. Another track, “Monster,” won Best Sound Engineer Recording.

items.title: Banks’ assets grow at end-July
items.description: ASSETS held by the Philippine banking industry expanded by over 10% year on year as of end-July, driven by sustained growth in lending and deposits, preliminary data from the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP) showed.

items.title: NGCP eyes completion of P23.5-B grid projects
items.description: THE National Grid Corp. of the Philippines (NGCP) is targeting the completion of six transmission projects worth about P23.5 billion by in the next 12 months as the grid operator works to address transmission reliability amid power supply constraints. At a briefing on Thursday, NGCP Assistant Vice-President Cynthia P. Alabanza said the company had already completed […]

items.title: Philippines not ready for AI use in capital markets
items.description: PHILIPPINE CAPITAL markets are not ready for the use of artificial intelligence (AI) for trading, advising, or prediction as the country’s investor base remains hesitant about new technologies, the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP) said. “Customers are resistant to the use [of AI in capital markets]. They’re hesitant, I think. They’re hesitant to use it […]

items.title: Toyota PHL expects vehicle output to fall this year
items.description: TOYOTA MOTOR Philippines Corp. (TMP) expects vehicle production to decline this year amid softer market demand that the automaker linked to higher oil prices stemming from the Middle East conflict. “It’s lower this year at maybe close to 60,000. Last year was about 63,000,” TMP Senior Vice-President for Marketing Division Sherwin T. Chua Lim said […]

items.title: Life insurers cover more than 50% of Filipinos
items.description: THE LIFE insurance industry covered more than half of the Philippine population as of the first half, driven by its growing branch and agency network. The Philippine Life Insurance Association, Inc. (PLIA) said in a statement that the sector now covers 63.5 million Filipinos, equivalent to around 55% of the country’s population. This was supported […]

items.title: Stuff to Do (09/18/26)
items.description: THE Design Center of the Philippines is marking a decade of the International Design Conference (IDC) with its 10th edition on Sept. 18 at the Foro de Intramuros, City of Manila, bringing together leading voices from the Philippines and around the world to look at how design can respond to the complexity and diversity of the world we live in.
